solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Greeter welcoming round first of party people with a reservation (4)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: a greeting that welcomes something takes it inside
indicatorNotes.first of: take only the opening letter of 'party'

annotation.surface: A host at the door greets the first guest to arrive at a party they had to book for.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' reads as a booking, but it is land set aside for a Native American people. O then P go between the H and I of HI.
annotation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people whose land is a reservation in Arizona.

entries.clue: Picked up all beef crumbs (4,3)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: what is picked up is heard, so a word is swapped for one that sounds the same

blocks.note: wholly = all, which sounds like HOLY

annotation.surface: Someone scoops every last crumb of beef off the plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' is not food here but a mild exclamation of surprise, just as HOLY COW is.
annotation.definitionFit: Both 'crumbs!' and 'holy cow!' are mild exclamations of surprise.

entries.clue: Hypocrite from work’s kisses upset fine female at home (9)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upsetting a group of letters turns it upside down, so it reads the other way

blocks.note: F = fine, as on a pencil grade

annotation.surface: An office two-face kisses colleagues at work, then upsets a fine woman at home.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'work' is a literary work: Seth Pecksniff is the hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit. F, F and IN are turned over to give NIFF.
annotation.definitionFit: Pecksniff is the sanctimonious hypocrite of Dickens's novel Martin Chuzzlewit.

entries.clue: Excited by a seal and mate, possibly in deep water (2,1,7)

blocks.note: up = excited, as in 'all het up'
to gum is to seal, as with an envelope
maté comes from a tree, so a mate is possibly a tree

annotation.surface: Someone is thrilled by a seal and its mate swimming in deep water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mate' is the South American maté plant, a kind of holly tree, not a partner; 'possibly' warns that it is just one example of a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a fix: a hunted possum up a gumtree is stuck, as a swimmer out of their depth is.

entries.clue: Cleans feathers on swan’s flanks (6)

indicatorNotes.flanks: the swan's letters stand on either side of another piece, holding it inside

blocks.note: a pen is a female swan, so swan's = PEN'S

annotation.surface: A bird grooms the plumage along a swan's sides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swan's flanks' looks like the outside letters of 'swan', but 'flanks' is a verb, and a pen is the word for a female swan.
annotation.definitionFit: A bird that preens cleans and tidies its feathers with its beak.

entries.clue: Periodically flog rubbish for one flipping dump (3,3,2)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: taking letters at regular intervals, here every other one
indicatorNotes.flipping: flipping a string turns it over, so it reads back to front

blocks.note: the first and third letters of FLOG

annotation.surface: Someone keeps trying to sell junk at a flipping rubbish tip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse on the dump; it is an instruction to turn FO + DIRT + EG back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dumping old furniture is disposing of it.

entries.clue: Minor actresses cast for director (6,8)

indicatorNotes.cast: casting throws the letters into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Bit-part actresses are chosen for a film director's picture.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is pure casting call, and 'cast' belongs to that picture, which is why it slips by as an instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American film director of Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

entries.clue: What pretender is expecting to do even as force is beginning to rise? (5)

annotation.definition: What pretender is expecting to do

indicatorNotes.even as: one thing happens even as another does, so the new letter comes in while the old goes out
indicatorNotes.beginning to: take only the opening letter of 'rise'

blocks.clueFragment: What pretender is expecting to do
blocks.note: a pretender feigns; this is the word worked on
R opens 'rise'; it takes the place of F

annotation.surface: A would-be king waits for the forces behind him to start an uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does two jobs: a pretender to the throne expects to reign, and a pretender also feigns. Swap FEIGN's F for R and you have REIGN.
annotation.definitionFit: A pretender to a throne claims it and expects one day to reign.

entries.clue: Spiky sort from Australia had nice moves (7)

indicatorNotes.moves: the letters move into a new order

annotation.surface: A prickly Australian showed off some neat dance steps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moves' reads as dance moves in the surface; here it tells you to reorder HAD NICE.
annotation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia.

entries.clue: Do not say no to bandage on part of foot (5,5,4)

blocks.note: to fancy something is to not say no to it
to dress a wound is to bandage it

annotation.surface: An instruction not to refuse a dressing for a sore foot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb opening an instruction, but it is the noun: a do is a party.
annotation.definitionFit: A do is a party, and a fancy dress ball is a party in costume.

entries.clue: Get some milk out and turn in after hours (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a turn is a stage act

annotation.surface: Someone fetches the milk from the fridge before going to bed late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn in' reads as going to bed; split the phrase, and 'turn' is a music-hall performance while 'in' is the container sign.
annotation.definitionFit: The medical verb for a mother or cow producing and releasing milk.

entries.clue: Dull American service is defended by leading pair of theologians (7)

indicatorNotes.is defended by: defenders stand around what they protect, so the outer letters wrap the rest

blocks.note: RN = Royal Navy, one of the armed services
the first two letters of THEOLOGIANS

annotation.surface: A boring church service in America is propped up by two senior theologians.
annotation.walkthrough: The theologians make 'service' look like worship, but it is one of the armed forces: the Royal Navy.
annotation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to dull, as a metal surface dulls or a reputation is dulled.

entries.clue: Old Cock Inn did teas brewed like some beers (4-11)

annotation.surface: A pub called the Old Cock Inn used to serve afternoon teas.
annotation.walkthrough: The Old Cock Inn sounds like a real pub name, so the eye takes the whole phrase as a unit; 'Old' only gives the O.
annotation.definitionFit: Cask-conditioned beer finishes fermenting in the cask it is served from, like real ale.

entries.clue: Feature of River Don ultimately lacking character (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately lacking: the word is missing its final letter

blocks.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

annotation.surface: A landmark on the River Don, a Yorkshire river, turns out to have no charm at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River Don' is a real river, which glues the words together; split them. 'Lacking character' also reads as a phrase, but 'character' is the definition: an odd person.
annotation.definitionFit: A character is an eccentric person, and a weirdo is an odd one.

entries.clue: Article on larvae characteristic of ill health somewhere in Africa (8)

blocks.note: a wan, pale look goes with poor health

annotation.surface: A medical paper on parasitic larvae that cause sickness in part of Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article on' places A after the rest, since in an across clue a piece that goes on another follows it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the landlocked southern African country is one of many places on that continent.

entries.clue: First-class menu with tiny changes very soon (3,6)

blocks.note: A = first-class, as in A1 or grade A

annotation.surface: A top restaurant will soon make small alterations to its menu.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tiny changes' reads as small alterations, but 'changes' is the verb working on MENU TINY.
annotation.definitionFit: Something coming any minute will happen very soon.

entries.clue: Get server’s attention, wanting one drink (3,5)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so a piece is removed

blocks.note: tap a waiter on the shoulder to get service
I = one, the Roman numeral; it is taken out

annotation.surface: A diner tries to catch the waiter's eye because they want something to drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting one drink' reads as ordering a drink; here 'wanting' is lacking, so the I goes from TAP WAITER.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: what comes from the kitchen faucet is one thing you can order to drink.

entries.clue: Sack staff in private? (8)

blocks.note: to sack a town is to plunder it, to rifle it
to staff a post is to man it

annotation.surface: A boss wonders whether to fire workers privately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sack staff' reads as firing employees; both words are verbs of a different kind. A private is a soldier of the lowest rank, and the question mark flags that a rifleman is only one sort.
annotation.definitionFit: A rifleman is a private soldier armed with a rifle.

entries.clue: Vehicle reversing over my new fur (7)

indicatorNotes.reversing: the word is read back to front

blocks.note: 'my!' and 'coo!' are both cries of surprise

annotation.surface: A car backs over someone's new fur coat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive but an exclamation, like COO. In a down clue, 'over' puts RAC above the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Raccoon is the fur of the North American raccoon, used for coats and hats.

entries.clue: He makes weapons that hurt you once invading Britain (6)

indicatorNotes.invading: an invader goes inside, so these letters sit within the others

blocks.note: 'ow!' is what you say when hurt
ye is the old form of 'you'

annotation.surface: An arms maker whose weapons wounded invaders of Britain long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as history, and fits: the English longbow, a bowyer's work, did hurt invaders once. 'Hurt' is the cry of pain, not the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A bowyer is a maker of bows for archery.

entries.clue: Works at last perhaps to add to residence housing despicable person (7)

annotation.definition: Works at last perhaps to add to

indicatorNotes.housing: a house holds what lives in it, so the outer letters go around the inner

annotation.surface: An estate agent's note on extending a house that shelters a scoundrel.
annotation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped form, not 'finally'; a cobbler working at one may put new heels on shoes.
annotation.definitionFit: A cobbler who reheels shoes works at a last to add new heels to them.

entries.clue: Reptiles biting top of umbelliferous plant (6)

indicatorNotes.biting: a biting mouth closes around something
indicatorNotes.top of: in a down clue the top is the first letter

annotation.surface: Crocodiles snap at the head of a plant of the carrot family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Umbelliferous plant' sounds like one botanical phrase; 'umbelliferous' only gives its U, and a crocus is not umbelliferous at all.
annotation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small spring-flowering plant grown from a corm.

entries.clue: Humour husband after son cracks puzzles? Fight! (5,6,4)

indicatorNotes.after: this piece comes after the rest
indicatorNotes.cracks: cracking into something means going inside it

blocks.note: crosswords are puzzles; the question mark admits this is one kind
S = son, placed between CROSS and WORDS

annotation.surface: A family row breaks out when the son solves the puzzles before his father can.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Son cracks puzzles' reads as a boy solving them; 'cracks' means breaking into, so the S splits the puzzles word in two.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from duelling, now used for any clash or argument, standing in for the imperative 'Fight!'.

entries.clue: Piece of gossip is somewhat recondite (2,3)

indicatorNotes.is somewhat: only some of the next word is used

blocks.note: five letters sit inside this word, after its first three

annotation.surface: A rumour that is rather obscure.
annotation.walkthrough: ON DIT is French, literally 'one says', borrowed into English for a rumour.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loan phrase, 'they say', used in English for a rumour.

entries.clue: Experienced sailor waving to lads touring lake (3,4)

indicatorNotes.waving: letters that wave move about into a new order
indicatorNotes.touring: going around something, so the letters surround it

annotation.surface: A veteran seaman waves to boys taking a trip around the lake.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged TO LADS goes around L; the surface's wave to the boys is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal term for a veteran seaman, from years spent in salt spray.

entries.clue: Particular habit set back you and me (7)

blocks.note: it set me back ten pounds = it cost me ten pounds
U sounds like 'you', as in text speak

annotation.surface: A peculiar habit has held back two friends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set back' looks like a reversal sign, but it is the verb meaning cost. 'Habit' is clothing, as a nun's habit is.
annotation.definitionFit: A habit is a distinctive outfit, and a costume is the dress of a particular kind.

entries.clue: Republican going into clear lead is an irritation (6,4)

indicatorNotes.going into: the letter goes inside the word

blocks.note: nett = clear, as in clear profit
a dog's lead is its leash

annotation.surface: A Republican opening a clear lead in the polls annoys the rivals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clear lead' reads as a winning margin in an election; 'lead' is the thing a dog is walked on. The double-T spelling of 'net' is British.
annotation.definitionFit: Nettle rash, or hives, is an itchy irritation of the skin.

entries.clue: Four different points in report (4)

blocks.note: the four compass points North, East, West, South

annotation.surface: A report makes four separate points.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'points' are compass points, not points in an argument.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a report on the radio is a piece of information about recent events.
